Inclusion & Access Commitment

Accessibility Statement

We believe historic ruins and green spaces belong to everyone. Here you will find an honest appraisal of our physical site terrain and our digital web accessibility standards.

On-Site Access

Physical Site Terrain & Honest Guidance

Grace Dieu Priory is a scheduled ancient monument situated in natural woodland and meadowland. Please review these realistic access notes before visiting.

Footpaths & Ground Surfaces

The path from the Bull’s Head car park follows a natural woodland trail with compacted earth, gravel sections, and occasional exposed tree roots. Within the priory precinct, the ground is grass meadow with uneven, weathered stone foundation thresholds.

Wheelchairs & Pushchairs

During dry summer weather, all-terrain wheelchairs and sturdy pushchairs can navigate the trail from the Bull's Head and traverse the priory grass meadow. After periods of heavy rain, woodland paths can become soft, muddy, and challenging for standard mobility aids.

Assistance Dogs Welcome

Trained guide dogs, hearing dogs, and medical assistance animals are warmly welcome across the entire site and ruins at all times. Fresh water bowls are available at the Bull's Head patron entrance.

Facilities & Lighting

As an open-air medieval ruin, there are no public toilets, running water, or artificial floodlights on the monument grounds. The nearest accessible customer facilities are situated at the Bull’s Head pub during opening hours.

Forthcoming Improvement: Accessible Pedestrian Footbridge

Following the Trust’s freehold purchase in 2024, plans are underway to construct a dedicated, step-free pedestrian footbridge linking Rusty Mary’s field directly into the priory cloister precinct, significantly improving step-free accessibility.

Digital Standards

Web Accessibility Standards (WCAG 2.2)

We strive to provide a website that meets Level AA conformance of the W3C Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2.2), with several criteria meeting Level AAA.

Design & Engineering Safeguards

This website has been built from the ground up with accessibility as a first-class requirement:

  • High Contrast Color Tokens: Deep Ivy Green (#2F4A3A) on Parchment (#F6F1E7) yields a 7.14:1 contrast ratio, exceeding WCAG AAA standards for normal body text.
  • Readable Base Typography: Body copy is styled at a minimum base of 18px in Source Sans 3 with generous line heights to facilitate effortless reading for older visitors.
  • Keyboard Navigability & Focus Rings: Every interactive link, button, and form control possesses visible high-contrast focus rings and supports full tab keyboard navigation.
  • Skip-to-Content: A persistent skip link is provided at the very top of each page for screen reader and keyboard users to bypass navigation menus.
  • Descriptive Text Equivalents: All photographic assets feature meaningful, contextual alt attributes; purely decorative vector icons are marked with aria-hidden="true".
  • Accessible Modals: Lightbox viewers and booking dialogs maintain ARIA focus management, trap tab navigation within the active overlay, and dismiss cleanly on the Escape key.

Accessibility Feedback & Tailored Visits

If you experience any difficulty accessing content on this website or wish to discuss tailored arrangements for a school group or visitor with limited mobility, please contact Malcolm Allsop or David Whitt. We will gladly advise on parking proximity and optimal route access.

Visitor Code

Leave No TracePlease take all of your litter home with you. There are no public waste bins on the ancient monument ruins.
Dog WalkersDogs welcome on leads. A dedicated bin is located at the Bull's Head car park for dog litter bags (strictly none on-site).
Strict Site Policy: Paranormal events and ghost walks are expressly forbidden by the Grace Dieu Priory Trust across the entire priory site and surrounding lands.
